summary: Regression testing after the security hardening (CSRF header guard, CORS, docs off, security headers, admin-only updater, secret scan). Backend: new suite test_iteration103_security_hardening.py, 23/23 passing. Also re-ran iteration102 (18/18), iteration4_auth_regression + iteration88 (13/13). UI (desktop): every requested write flow works with the X-Requested-With header and no 403s: login, creating 2 TEST_ companies (onboarding + Aziende), Padre dialog save (badge shown), saving Dati azienda, AI switch off/on, AI credits dialog -> package -> redirect to the Stripe checkout (test mode), creating a party, saving a draft invoice, uploading a passive XML (imported), a manual Prima nota entry (balanced and saved), logout. Secret scan of HEAD found no real credentials or MongoDB connection strings with credentials. The admin password does appear in git history.

minor.issue: MONGO_URL is missing, but docker-compose.yml requires it (${MONGO_URL:?...}), so `docker compose up` stops with an error until the user adds it. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and EMERGENT_LLM_KEY are also missing, so on a fresh install AI credits and the webhook fail.
No add_header security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, CSP) on the SPA/HTML responses and no `server_tokens off`. The FastAPI middleware only protects /api responses.

The mongo service runs without authentication (no MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME/PASSWORD). This is acceptable only because no port is published. Document this, or add auth and put the credentials in MONGO_URL from .env.

issues: The Data field uses the browser's native date input (mm/dd/yyyy shown in the US locale) instead of a shadcn calendar. This predates this iteration.

action_items: SECURITY: the admin password value (the one in memory/test_credentials.md) is in git history in 14 commits (old test files deleted on purpose are still in history, e.g. commits 0c6e93c, 8e38f1b). HEAD is clean. Tell the user to change ADMIN_PASSWORD/the admin password on the production server, or rewrite history (git filter-repo) before pushing the repository anywhere.
Add MONGO_URL="mongodb://mongo:27017" (and the STRIPE_*/EMERGENT_LLM_KEY placeholders) to deploy/.env.example
Optional hardening: add security headers and `server_tokens off` to deploy/nginx.conf for non-API responses

tests/test_iteration2_features.py is stale and fails (13 tests: relies on the preseeded session test_session_T1_admin_approved and the single-company `company` collection). It is unrelated to the hardening; rewrite it or remove it.
critical_code_review_comments: The CSRF guard is correct: it checks POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE on /api/*, exempts only /api/stripe/webhook, and requires the exact value 'invoix' (another value -> 403). GET requests are not affected.
CORS filters out '*', allow_credentials=True and explicit origins. A foreign Origin gets no ACAO header. Same-origin preflight returns 200 with ACAO equal to the app URL.
docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url are None: /docs, /openapi.json and /redoc return 404 on localhost:8001.
Headers on /api responses: nosniff, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, HSTS (when COOKIE_SECURE), Cache-Control no-store, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP.

There are only 3 places outside lib/api.js that send writes (ConsulenteIA fetch, FirmaDdtPublic axios.post, lib/api) and all of them send the header. No other raw fetch or axios write calls were found.
ai_crediti.py now uses os.environ.get('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY') with no hardcoded sk_test fallback, which resolves the iteration 102 comment.

The secret grep (excluding node_modules, .git, backend/.env, memory/test_credentials.md) found only placeholders ('cambia-questa-password', 'password-ftp' in the *.env.example files), mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017 without credentials (Windows example and docs), and dummy test passwords for TEST users in the test files. No API keys, Stripe keys or LLM keys were found.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/conftest.py (new: injects X-Requested-With: invoix into every requests.Session, so the whole legacy regression suite works again; without it all older suites fail with 403)

success_rate.backend: 100% (23/23 new + 31/31 re-run legacy suites; iteration2 suite is stale, not a regression)

seed_data_creation: Temporary data, all deleted at the end: users test-user-t103-admin/oper (backend) and test-user-t103-ui (UI login, bcrypt hash set via mongosh), companies TEST_T103 Srl and TEST_T103 UI Padre/Cliente Srl plus their parties, invoice, passive invoice, coa_* data, coge entry and payment_transactions. DB is back to 0 companies and 1 user (the admin). The admin login test (it reads ADMIN_PASSWORD from env) left one extra session row in user_sessions for the admin; the account itself was not changed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && set -a && . ./.env && . ../frontend/.env && set +a && pytest tests/test_iteration103_security_hardening.py -v -n 0. The conftest.py auto-adds the CSRF header to every requests session. To check a 403, pop the header from the session or pass headers={'X-Requested-With': None}. WARNING: the clean() in test 103 deletes companies matching /^TEST_T103/, so give UI-created companies a different prefix (e.g. TEST_T103UI won't help either; use TEST_UI103). UI login: insert a TEST admin user with a bcrypt password_hash via mongosh. The DB has no companies, so the first login shows the 'Crea la prima azienda' onboarding.
